title: Web app with sign-in and a database
fits: A web app people sign in to, with its own data: client portals, booking tools, dashboards, small business software, internal tools.
notFor: more than one server at once (the database is one file on one server)
a site with no sign-in and no stored data (use the website recipe)
a team that already knows and wants another framework

stack.why: One language for screens and server; types catch mistakes before tests do.

stack.choice: SvelteKit 3 with Svelte 5 and the Node adapter
stack.why: Pages render on the server and forms work without JavaScript; built-in cross-site form protection.

stack.choice: SQLite through better-sqlite3, with Drizzle for queries and migrations
stack.why: One file, no database server to run or pay for; typed queries that can't be injected.

stack.choice: Better Auth (email and password), set up by the official SvelteKit add-on
stack.why: Sessions, password hashing and the database tables come ready and tested.

stack.choice: Vitest (server tests and component tests in a real browser) and Playwright
stack.why: Both come wired in by the official setup tool.

scaffold: npx --yes sv@1.7.1 create app --template minimal --types ts --add eslint vitest="usages:unit,component" playwright="demo:no" sveltekit-adapter="adapter:node" drizzle="database:sqlite+sqlite:better-sqlite3" better-auth="demo:password" --no-install --package-manager npm

after.do: The setup adds a sign-in demo under src/routes/demo/. Keep it only until the first sign-in feature replaces it, then delete it.

host.name: Any host that runs a container (or Node.js) with a lasting disk, running one copy
host.deploy: npm ci, npm run build, then node build with ORIGIN set to the public address and DATABASE_URL pointing at a file on the lasting disk. Set up by /starter-kit:launch; not part of the recipe test. The recipe's container files (presets.mjs --container) make it portable; /starter-kit:launch compares two or three hosts' current prices then (decision D9).
host.preview: a second copy with its own database file and test keys only.

accounts.name: GitHub
accounts.why: Holds the code and runs the checks on every push.

accounts.name: A hosting account (one server with a lasting disk)
accounts.why: Runs the app and keeps the database file.

accounts.name: An email-sending service
accounts.when: when password reset or emails are built
accounts.why: Sign-in emails need a sender that isn't marked as spam.

accounts.name: A domain name
accounts.why: A real address instead of the host's.

settings.name: DATABASE_URL
settings.why: Where the database file lives. Locally local.db; live, a file on the lasting disk.

settings.name: ORIGIN
settings.why: The app's public address. If it is wrong, every form post is refused as cross-site.

settings.name: BETTER_AUTH_SECRET
settings.why: Signs sign-in sessions. 32 or more random characters, different for each copy, never committed.

notes: This is SvelteKit 3, not 2: settings and the adapter live in vite.config.ts (there is no svelte.config.js); environment variables are declared in src/env.ts with defineEnvVars and read from '$app/env/private' (server) or '$app/env' (not '$env/static/...').
Imports use the '#lib/...' alias from package.json "imports" (with the .ts extension), not '$lib'.
Svelte 5 runes only: $state, $derived, $props, $effect. No 'export let', no '$:' and no stores for local state (the config forces runes mode).
Code that touches the database or secrets lives in src/lib/server/ or in +page.server.ts / +server.ts files. Never import it from a component.
Every load function and form action that reads or changes data checks event.locals.user itself, and filters by that user's id in the query. Hiding a link is not protection.
Database changes: edit src/lib/server/db/schema.ts, then npm run db:generate and commit the migration. db:push is only for a throwaway local database.
After changing Better Auth's settings or plugins, run npm run auth:schema again; sveltekitCookies must stay the last plugin.
Component tests are files named *.svelte.spec.ts and run in a real browser; plain logic tests are *.spec.ts and run in Node. Vitest requires every test to make at least one assertion.
Playwright browsers are installed once per computer (npx playwright install chromium); the test command never downloads them.
SQLite means one running copy of the app. Back up the database file, never run two servers on it, and move to a database server before planning a second copy.
The setup tool installs with ^ ranges; the committed package-lock.json is what pins the versions. Always commit it and install with npm ci.

container.why: One portable image for any host that runs containers with a lasting disk (decision D9: no host is built in).

Dockerfile: # Built and checked weekly by the starter kit's recipe job. One copy of the app; the database file lives on the /data volume.
RUN npm run build && npm prune --omit=dev

container.run: docker run -p 3000:3000 -v app-data:/data -e ORIGIN=https://<your address> -e BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=<32+ random characters> <image>
